name: http
task:
Serve `GET /` with `200 OK`, `Content-Type: text/plain` and the 14-byte body `Hello, World!
` (with Content-Length) over HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, with the language's std HTTP server.

skip.c: no std HTTP (C's std has no sockets)
skip.rust: no std HTTP (std::net is TCP only; hyper and axum are crates)

models.mk: tasks (std.http.Serve, one task and one arena per connection, MK_CARRIERS=8)
models.zig: OS threads (std.http.Server, one Io.Group.concurrent thread per connection)

notes: The generator is tools/bench's own (httpbench.go): a raw HTTP/1.1 client on Go's net.Conn, one goroutine per connection, rather than net/http.Client, so it spends little per request; connections close with a reset, so no TIME_WAIT sockets pile up between sweeps. 1,000 connections hold 2,000 sockets on the machine at once, below the owner's 10,000 cap.
